subject: history
source_note: Topic structure follows the Cambridge IGCSE History specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

units.name: Core content — Option B: The 20th century

connections.why: The breakdown of interwar diplomacy leads directly into Cold War and Gulf tensions
The Treaty of Versailles and the rise of Hitler are central to both the core and the depth study
Both trace the collapse of a regime and the rise of a totalitarian dictatorship between the wars
Stalin's USSR became one of the two superpowers that defined the Cold War
German aggression and appeasement drove the failure of collective security in the 1930s
Both contrast how democratic and communist states responded to depression and crisis
The Wall Street Crash and Depression destabilised democracies including Weimar Germany
Both trace the rise of communist regimes and the tools they used to control society
Communist China became a major actor in the global Cold War balance of power
Both examine deep-rooted conflicts over land, rights and segregation in the 20th century
Middle Eastern conflict became entangled with superpower rivalry and Gulf tensions
Apartheid and decolonisation were shaped by and tested the international order
